target_customer: Urban consumers in Mexico who book at-home massage, nails, barbering and beauty, plus businesses booking spa services for offices, events and hotels
problem: Quality spa and beauty services at home are hard to find and trust in Latin America. Providers are informal and customers worry about safety and quality.
business_model: Two-sided marketplace taking a commission on services booked through the app, plus packages, memberships, gift cards and corporate bookings
product_category: On-demand at-home beauty and wellness services marketplace

founders.name: Ana Ramos
founders.background_notes: YC page describes her as a former early-stage VC investor. Employer and education not found in an opened source.

founders.name: Luis Enrique Vazquez
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a programmer focused on mobile apps who worked as a developer for small companies and large corporations in several Mexican cities. No employer names or education given.

founders.name: Leonel Campos
founders.background_notes: Named as a founder with Ramos and Vazquez in the June 2023 LatamList article, which gives no background. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Scape
competitors.what: Mexican on-demand app for at-home massage and wellness services
competitors.traction_then: Founded 2019 per a later profile. No 2021 traction found.

competitors.name: Singu
competitors.what: Brazilian on-demand at-home massage and beauty app, named by Ramos as a player delivering at-home services in LatAm
competitors.traction_then: Founded 2015 in Sao Paulo. Natura investment reported in 2020.
competitors.funding_then: about 3.03M USD total per CB Insights

technical_complexity.rationale: A two-sided booking app with scheduling, payments and provider vetting. Standard marketplace engineering; the hard part was operations, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Copyable app. The moat is a vetted provider network and local density, which take time and cash to build city by city.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge by the sources found. Competitors stayed separate marketplaces.

market_need_then: At-home services demand rose in Latin America around 2020 and 2021 as people avoided salons during the pandemic. No spend figures were found in opened sources.

branding.domain_note: Uses glitzi.com.mx, a country code domain, not the .com. No acquisition note found.

identity.logo: not described by any opened source
identity.visual_style: Premium beauty positioning on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish copy that is warm and indulgent, for example relax and treat yourself from the comfort of home

branding.community_and_virality: Site shows a rewards program, referral program and coach directory. No press on the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: Pleasant and easy to say, but no source shows press, merch or community around the name. Brand is mostly functional marketplace branding.

outcome_analysis: Glitzi is still active and has operated in Mexico City, Monterrey, Guadalajara, Queretaro, Tulum and Merida per its site. It raised a 2.8M dollar round in June 2023 after YC and reported about 700 providers and 170,000 services booked. No later round, exit or shutdown was found. The pandemic shift to at-home services helped, while thin defensibility and city-by-city operations remain the open risks.
notes: Funding: stated by LatamList and repeated by Seedtable, TechGist Africa and Team France Export. Seedtable labels it seed; LatamList says venture round, so stage is other. Founding year is 2019 per the YC page and LatamList; CB Insights says 2017 and another profile says 2020. Competitor sources for Scape and Singu are dated after or before the batch and were found in search results without being opened; Scape existence in 2021 rests on a founded 2019 statement. An outcome search for acquisition, layoffs or shutdown returned nothing about Glitzi. Search snippets say Ramos was an Investment Manager at Vorwerk Ventures, which no opened source confirmed, so it is not recorded.
